title: Why does a planner have a subscription fee?
body: The product looks great, and I have major ADHD, and want a tool that will better help me to organize my day-to-day life than apps like Google Keep/Tasks, which don’t have very much functionality beyond basic note taking and check-list creation. That said, I can’t justify spending $6/month on a planner app. If you go and buy a paper-based organizer you don’t go back to the store and pay $6 every month. I could maybe agree with a small annual fee, but beyond a one time charge, I find it aggravating that app-developers squeeze consumers for monthly payments on such simple products. I would have no problem paying $20 for the product. There is no way that you need to charge $6 to both make a profit, and maintain the app - it’s a planner, not helping me to split the atom.
author: Fmonthlysubscriptionfees

title: Great application
body: This is probably the most feature-packed everything tracking application I have see to date. The UI is refined and you actually feel happy when using it. Kudos to the developer
author: Bennyhawk

title: Nice app
body:
This is a very nice app. 

For developers: There is one annoying feature/shortcut. With emacs keybindings (default in MacOS), Ctrl-n is used to go down one line. This app creates a new journal entry/note instead. Since you usually move by several lines up and down at atime, this creates multiple new notes/journal entreis that I need then to delete... I would really appreciate if you could replace Ctrl-n with CMD-n as every other app does. Thanks!
author: Random user xyz

title: Steep learning curve
body: I have used Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Structured, Todoist, and others. Never had an issue with creating a task. With Lunatask, I could only figure out how to create habits. Habits are great, but I also need to get tasks done. I found it very confusing and I stayed for the whole tutorial. Was drawn to the ADHD-friendly perspective but not very user friendly. Going back to Google. Plus, no app for iphone. For us ADHD folks... out of sight, out of mind.
